subject: [PATCH] mm/madvise: reclaim isolated folios if PTE restart fails

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Andrew Morton expressed frustration that the patch did not provide a clear outcome after encountering an error, leaving it unclear whether the machine crashed or if there was a permanent memory leak.

Reviewer Andrew Morton expressed frustration with the need to repeatedly explain kernel locking rules, specifically pointing out that vma->vm_mm is not a valid lock argument for pte_offset_map_lock() and requested correction.

Reviewer Andrew Morton suggested updating the LLM prompts to check for userspace-visible runtime effects and stable-kernel-rules compliance, and requested that Gregory Price share the updated prompt so he can add it to his signature.
reviews.raw_body:
aw man, you got so close then left us hanging.

So what happened next?  Machine crashed?  Permanent leak?

---

#include "Documentation/process/stable-kernel-rules.rst"

(sorry, getting snarky.  I'm saying this stuff 100x/day at present and

2026-09-14.patch_summary: This patch addresses a concurrency issue in the Linux kernel's madvise functionality. When MADV_PAGEOUT is used to collect isolated folios, a concurrent operation can remove or replace the PTE table while the lock is dropped, causing pte_offset_map_lock() to return NULL and bypassing reclaim_pages(). The patch routes this failure through the existing cleanup path, ensuring that any collected folios are reclaimed or put back. This fix prevents a situation where isolated folios remain off the LRU with elevated references.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged a permanent memory leak issue, citing that nr_isolated_anon increases reliably but doesn't decrease when the process dies.

Author acknowledged that the patch's original issue of a potential memory leak is not as severe as initially thought, and agreed to rephrase the problem in terms of how to observe it rather than fix it immediately.

Permanent leak.

nr_isolated_anon increases reliably and does not decrease when the
process dies.

---

I typically (re)write (or at least heavily edit) the messages to ensure I
actually understand what's going on.  I'll update my brainmeats.

I get it though, rather than permanent leak say how to observe said leak

~Gregory

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lorenzo questioned the necessity of the reschedule path, suggesting it's 'sketchy' and proposing to remove it, referencing a modern approach that avoids cond_resched() and friends.

Reviewer Lorenzo expressed strong disagreement and disappointment with the quality of the code, stating it's 'some of the absolute worst' they've seen in mm, but did not provide specific technical feedback or suggestions.

Reviewer Lorenzo (ARM) questioned the placement of a new label/goto in madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() and suggested an alternative approach to avoid duplication, recommending that the existing condition be moved before the reclaim_pages() call.
reviews.raw_body:
Is this reschedule path even necessary? It's pretty bloody sketchy.

I thought the modern approach (TM) was to not do cond_resched() and friends so
can we actually look at removing this?

---

This function is truly some of the absolute worst code I've read in
mm. Shocking.

---

Seems odd to put this here for a condition that explicitly guarantees
!start_pte? It should be before the if (pageout) reclaim_pages(...);
surely?

I honestly wonder whether, rather than adding yet another label/goto into this
absolute bloody mess, whether we should just live with a bit of duplication and do:

	if (!start_pte) {
		if (pageout)
			reclaim_pages(&folio_list);
		return 0;
	}

I actually think that'd be clearer at this point than throwing in some more
indirection.

That's for the backport but somebody needs to rework this entire bloody
function going forwards...

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary:
Author agrees that the madvise function is in need of improvement, acknowledging it's 'horrendous' and confirming their own conviction that madvise requires attention.

Author acknowledged that the use of a goto statement in madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() is problematic and may be considered worse than the original label, but did not commit to changing it.

Author acknowledges that madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() has significant issues, but expresses difficulty in generalizing page table walkers across the kernel and does not commit to a fix.
reviews.raw_body:
relevant meme: https://i.imgur.com/W0N40BK.png

No argument here. This function in particular is really horrendous.

I think i'm now 4 or 5 stacks deep on the "Thanks for fixing a bug, but
while reviewing your fix sashiko found yet another CVE-worthy bug".

I'm convinced (like you below) madvise needs some attention.

---

I wanted to prevent any future use of the label from skipping the
start_pte check.  The function is so bad I was err'ing on the side
of being a bit defensive without making it worse.

I suppose reasonable to say the goto is worse.

---

The longer I look at madvise, the more I think it is a wart on mm/
as-written.  A userland-driven page table walker that requires all
the special-casing of Yooj Pages, zone device, swap, soft leafs, a
bunch of tlb flushing 5-tabs deep...

Scary surface.

I've been trying to think about how we might make this more reasonable,
but generalizing the different walkers across mm is pretty hard.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that the feedback was unclear due to the complexity of the function and promises to re-evaluate the code, but does not commit to making changes.
